items.title: Sheryl Bailey interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, July 24, 2023
items.q: But I explain this in the course is that that book really helped me develop a language.

ctx.x: And sometimes I wonder, is that assumption correct or were they doing what John Abercrombie described as finger wiggling and this is what came out. In other words there’s a certain amount of happy accidents I think, in improvising. Does it need to be explained?

I mean I don’t know, I mean we can never say, we can never know what a player is thinking, ever, right? What was going through their mind. But I mean for instance I mean if you see something, for me I mean I think I also use transcription to say, “Oh wow that’s a really cool sound on that C 7 chord. What is that?” And then just find the concept behind it you know. Now whether that’s what they were thinking — what Joe Pass was thinking that? Probably not. It’s just a sound that he’s internalized. It’s part of his…

Oh I love it. No I just love it because I use that word magic a lot and you just put it in a wonderful context. When you were first on that path of learning/creating your own diary of licks and so forth, were you mostly playing in one key?
